finding: expect_rejected() returns silently on both the except-ContractError path and the fallthrough after a successful (non-rejecting) validate_contract_value call, so a mutation that the validator fails to reject never raises — the guard is vacuous and always 'passes'.

mirror_executed only skips whole-line comments (stripped.startswith('#')) and then regex-matches tests/verify_\w+\.py anywhere on the remaining lines, so a trailing inline comment like `cmd  # tests/verify_new.py` gets counted as executed even though nothing runs it.

instructionSha256/approvedChangeSha256 checks (lines 10-11, 17-18) recompute the hash from userInstruction/approvedChange and compare only against route.get("instructionSha256")/route.get("approvedChangeSha256") from the same document, with no pinned literal to anchor against — a self-authenticating check where editing the text and its declared hash together still passes.

the added check's boolean condition `entry_outside_cf <= on_disk` never references historical_core_full (it appears only in the failure message), so the check named 'the CORE/FULL outside set is the historical one' does not actually verify equality/derivation against the historical CORE/FULL parse and can pass even under a name substitution.

line `check(..., name not in local)` compares the extension-included basename (name = Path(suite).name, e.g. 'verify_foo.py') against `local`, which (per the sibling suite-name sets built elsewhere in this file) holds extension-stripped suite names, so the membership test can never be true and the 'not silently also in the mirror' guard is vacuous.

the reason/reproduce check only requires row['reproduce'] to be a non-empty string (bool(...).strip()) with no check that it is executable rather than a placeholder, so a value like `... --phase <phase>` passes despite never actually reproducing anything.
